elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Rendered Article XXII now reads "The Licensor shall have no right of first refusal, no right to match, and no other right to be notified of or to receive any terms that the Licensee offers to or receives from a third party." The original Licensee-side obligation to give written notice of a bona fide third-party offer and to allow Licensor a five-business-day Exercise Period to take that offer is deleted in operative text (not merely promised in the comment), so no matching/most-favoured-offer mechanic burdening Licensee (Customer) survives. Under the rule boundary, a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic is assessed as MFN, and it has been eliminated.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no Customer-side MFN/right-to-match obligation exists at all, so there is no scope to confine to a defined product. A zero-scope obligation cannot exceed a defined-product limit.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the deleted mechanic ran "During the term of this Agreement" (36 months plus a possible renewal), but it no longer exists in the rendered clause, so no duration limit is required.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the disclosure/matching obligation removed there is no comparison exercise to carve out from.

elements.element: Minimality of the conforming second sentence
elements.evidence: The follow-on sentence was not merely conformed; it was broadened from "the Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party" to "Without notice to or the consent of the Licensor, the Licensee shall have the right to consummate any transaction with a third party." The original clause imposed no consent requirement, and it addressed only the specific noticed transaction.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative text extinguishes the Licensee-side notice/most-favoured-offer and matching mechanic, which is the single preferred element. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation at the fallback level (no defined product, term-long duration, no like-for-like carve-out).

Minimality defect 1 — scope creep in the conforming sentence: replace "Without notice to or the consent of the Licensor, the Licensee shall have the right to consummate any transaction with a third party" with either straight deletion of the sentence or a narrow conforming version (e.g. "The Licensee may consummate the transaction with the third party."). Striking "or the consent of the Licensor" is required: the deleted Article XXII never conditioned any transaction on Licensor consent, so the new words create a fresh, unnecessary consent-free permission covering all third-party transactions.

Minimality defect 2 — surplus negative covenant: the added tail "and no other right to be notified of or to receive any terms that the Licensee offers to or receives from a third party" goes beyond removing the obligation and is unnecessary once the mechanic and its defined terms ("Right of First Refusal", "Exercise Period") are deleted. A simple deletion of the Article, or a one-line "Intentionally omitted / Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match", achieves the element without new operative breadth.

Intent risk to police before sending: the broadened "without ... the consent of the Licensor ... any transaction with a third party" language could contradict any retained assignment or change-of-control consent provision elsewhere in the Agreement (an effective override of that clause). Confirm the assignment article and, if a consent requirement is retained, narrow this sentence so the two do not conflict. Aside from this risk, no dangling defined terms or cross-references remain, since "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" were defined only in the deleted text.
Margin comment is accurate and appropriately scoped; no separate flagging of the same term under ASSIGN should occur unless the assignment rule is independently breached.
